extracted.intended_audience: legal professionals (attorneys, judges, law firms) doing patent litigation analytics and research
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and interpreting data-driven analytics about U.S. patent litigation (district courts, PTAB, federal appeals) including definitions, tags, timing, outcomes, and party/firm/judge activity to inform litigation strategy and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a Patent Case
rubrics_metrics.description: A case with one or more claims involving patent infringement, invalidity, or unenforceability brought under 35 USC § 271. False marking, inventorship, or contract cases are not included in the patent case type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine which matters are included in the patent dataset; explicitly excludes false marking, inventorship, and contract cases. Applies across district courts, federal appeals, and PTAB-related analytics in this report.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-Volume Plaintiff (HVP) Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: High-Volume Plaintiff — filers meaning that the party has filed at least 10 patent cases (excluding ANDA cases) within a 365-day period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a party meets the threshold, the HVP tag applies to all of the party's patent cases (excluding ANDA cases) in which the party is a plaintiff (or defendant in a declaratory judgment case), regardless of when the cases were filed. The classification is behavior-based (to avoid subjective labels like NPE/PAE).

rubrics_metrics.name: ANDA Tag / Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ANDA — patent cases prompted by the filing of an ANDA or paper NDA that includes a Paragraph IV Certification (incentivized by the Hatch-Waxman Act's first to file exclusivity provisions for prospective generic drug makers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a case tag to identify ANDA-originating patent litigation. ANDA cases are analyzed separately for timing and resolution patterns (e.g., different median times, higher rates of consent judgments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Tagging System (Lex Machina case filter system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina uses machine learning and natural language processing to create case tags that identify certain claims in a case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tags (e.g., ANDA, High-Volume Plaintiff, design patent) enable filtering and comparison across cohorts. The platform supplements ML with human review and allows users to apply additional tags in their research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Cases Filed (volume/time-series)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track patent case filings by year (e.g., 2015–2024) and by subcategories (general patent, excluding HVPs, ANDA, design patents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report compares three-year period (2022–2024) to historical figures and three-year averages; highlights rebounds/declines and percent changes year-over-year. Charts/figures present absolute counts and enable trend interpretation for planning and budgeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Districts (ranking by cases filed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank federal district courts by number of patent cases filed (e.g., E.D. Tex., W.D. Tex., D. Del.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show counts for multi-year windows (2022–2024) and total percent share. Useful for venue strategy and identifying regional concentration of litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Judges (ranking by cases assigned)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank individual judges by the number of patent cases assigned over a given period (e.g., three-year totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides counts by year and multi-year totals and percent of population. Enables judge-specific strategy (timing, motion practice) because judge assignment materially affects caseload and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Parties (plaintiffs and defendants) by case volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify parties (entities) with the highest numbers of patent cases filed or named as defendants over a period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables include per-year counts, multi-year totals, and districts involved. Highlights trends among monetizers, operating companies, and repeat defendants for adverse-party assessment and business-development purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Active Law Firms and Attorneys (plaintiff and defendant side)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank law firms and individual attorneys by number of patent cases in which they appear for plaintiffs or defendants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Displays per-year counts, totals, district coverage, and percentage of cases involving HVPs. Lex Machina normalizes counsel names and extracts counsel data from dockets; useful for assessing opposing counsel experience and prospecting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing Metrics (time-to-event)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing analytics measure time from filing to key milestones (e.g., claim construction hearing, summary judgment decision, trial, termination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as medians and visualized with box plots. Example medians for non-ANDA terminated cases (2022–2024): claim construction hearing = 410 days; summary judgment = 848 days; trial = 1,040 days; termination = 208 days. ANDA medians differ (e.g., claim construction 482 days, trial 837 days). Timing ranges vary widely; additional factors (issues, venue, parties) should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box Plot Interpretation for Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Box plots summarize distributions using five statistics: median, lower and upper quartiles (box bounds), and whiskers/outliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Median is center line. Box encloses middle 50% (25th–75th percentiles). Compressed box = more consistency; elongated box = more spread. Whiskers extend to bounds; points beyond 1.5× IQR are outliers. Lex Machina uses box plots to convey timing expectations and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Resolution Categories and Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify terminated district-court patent cases into resolution types: claimant wins (default judgment, consent judgment, judgment on the pleadings, summary judgment, trial, judgment as a matter of law, etc.), claim defendant wins (same subtypes), likely settlement, procedural resolution (dismissal, consolidation, severance, transfer, stay, MDL, sealed), and open/no resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify proportions (e.g., ~90% of non-ANDA district cases resolved by settlements or procedural rulings in 2022–2024). Distinguish ANDA patterns (more consent judgments, fewer default judgments, defendants win trials more often in ANDA). Use granular categories to understand typical endgames in different case types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Appellate Outcomes and Reversal Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Track appellate resolutions (appellant win, appellee win, reversed, affirmed, affirmed/reversed in part) and compute reversal rate for appeals decided on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: patent-originating appeals (terminated 2022–2024) had a 36% reversal rate for merits decisions; reversal rate calculated as (Reversed + Affirmed/Reversed in Part) ÷ (Reversed + Affirmed/Reversed in Part + Affirmed). Present counts and percent breakdowns to assess appellate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings by Judgment Event
rubrics_metrics.description: Record whether cases have findings at various judgment events and the nature of those findings (Infringement, No Infringement, Invalidity, No Invalidity, Unenforceability, No Unenforceability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single case may have findings at multiple events (e.g., summary judgment and trial). Claim-construction orders are counted as summary-judgment findings for the purposes of the report. Use findings data to estimate likelihoods of outcomes at stages and by judge/court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Invalidity Reasons (granular legal grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Track specific legal grounds for invalidity findings: 101 Subject Matter, 102 Anticipation/Novelty, 102(f) Derivation (pre-AIA), 103 Obviousness, 112 Definiteness, 112 Enablement, 112 Written Description, defective correction statutes (132,251,255,305), obviousness-type double patenting, or No Invalidity Reason Specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report highlights which grounds are most common (e.g., subject-matter ineligibility / §101 most frequent, often at judgment on the pleadings; indefiniteness often reached during claim construction). Break down findings by judgment event to see where specific grounds prevail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages Metrics and Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure number of cases with damages awards, total damages awarded by year (excluding fees, costs, interest), and reversed damages (cases/amounts reversed on appeal). Annotated damage types include Reasonable Royalty, Lost Profits, Enhanced Damages, Attorneys' Fees/Costs, Other/Mixed Damage Types, and Prejudgment Interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures show per-year counts and monetary totals (e.g., 2024: 94 cases, $4,351M awarded, excluding reversed awards). Amount columns include only awards not reversed on appeal; appeal reversals may change recent figures. Use damage-type breakdowns to understand award composition and trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Petitions by Type and Year
rubrics_metrics.description: Track number of PTAB petitions filed annually by petition type (IPR, PGR, CBM) from 2015–2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe long-term trends and policy-driven shifts (e.g., CBM filings ended in Sept 2020). Use annual counts to assess PTAB activity and ecosystem changes related to USPTO/Federal Circuit guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Institution Rate and Trial Flow
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure institution decisions and downstream trial outcomes: percent of petitions denied institution vs. instituted, and final trial outcomes (all claims unpatentable, all claims upheld, mixed findings, amended claims, patent owner disclaimed, settled, procedurally dismissed, joined to other trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example flow for trials terminated 2022–2024 (out of 3,903 petitions): Denied institution 805 (21%); Instituted 2,278 (58%); Procedurally dismissed pre/post institution; Settled; Final outcomes include Petitioner Win 1,047 (27%), Patent Owner Win 2,447 (63%), Partial 219 (6%). Note policy influence (e.g., Fintiv doctrine changes) and that institution rates rose since 2022 but policy reversals (March 2025 director review) may shift future rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Party and Firm Activity Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify most active PTAB petitioners, patent owners, and law firms by trials petitioned, with associated metrics (number of patents at issue, number of APJs presiding, percent of cases where firm represented petitioner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tables list per-year and total counts (2022–2024). Use counts, patent counts, and APJ coverage to assess experience and specialization in PTAB practice (e.g., Fish & Richardson leading in trials petitioned).

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Appeal Outcomes and Reversal Rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Track appellate resolutions originating from PTAB (appellant win, appellee win, reversed, affirmed, affirmed/reversed in part) and compute reversal rate for merits decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: PTAB appeals terminated 2022–2024 showed a 22% reversal rate (calculated analogously to district-court appellate reversal calculation). Present counts and percent breakdowns to evaluate appellate trends for PTAB-originating matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Sources, Processing, and Update Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lex Machina uses data from PACER and other court sources; raw data is extracted, cleaned, normalized, tagged, and annotated using machine learning plus technology-assisted attorney review. The platform updates daily; report numbers are as of publication and may change as PACER adds new cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodology notes specific supplements: correcting errors, normalizing judges/parties/firms/attorneys, extracting counsel records absent from dockets, tagging/categorizing cases, and annotating resolutions, damages, and dispositive rulings. Users should treat the report as a snapshot of a dynamic dataset and consult the platform for up-to-date counts.
